name: the srgb branch stops scaling, so a normalised colour reads as near-black and every ratio is fiction
expect: color(srgb ...) is NORMALISED and scales UP, not down

name: an unparseable colour is GUESSED as black instead of refusing
edits:
raise CannotRun(f"unparseable computed colour {css!r} — the measurement cannot proceed on a "
                    f"colour it does not understand, and guessing one would be a fabricated number")
expect: an unparseable colour REFUSES rather than guessing — returned instead of refusing

name: compositing ignores alpha, so translucent text is scored on its declared colour
expect: a fully transparent foreground becomes the background

name: the large-text carve-out applies to everything, so small text is held to 3.0
expect: 16px normal weight needs 4.5

name: the CROSSED branch is severed, so an element that fell below AA is reported as merely WORSENED and the reader cannot tell the two apart
expect: ...and the message says CROSSED

name: a NEW element below AA is admitted silently instead of reported
expect: a NEW failing site is reported rather than admitted silently

name: the corpus rule accepts fragments, so chromeless files with no palette are measured
expect: a chromeless fragment is NOT

name: siblings are merged again, so a passing one can cross below AA behind a failing one
expect: ...and are numbered in document order, so the numbering is reproducible

name: gradient-backed text is scored against the colour beneath, which no reader sees
edits: scored = [s for s in samples if not s.get("bg_uncertain")]
expect: a gradient-backed site is not counted as below AA, however bad its nominal ratio

name: the VANISHED advisory is silenced unconditionally, so a baselined page absent from a run says nothing
expect: a baselined site NOT measured this run is reported

name: a baselined site that leaves the verdict on a gradient is dropped silently again
edits: unscored = [s for s in samples if s.get("bg_uncertain") and sample_key(s) in prior]
expect: a BASELINED site that becomes gradient-backed is reported, not silently dropped

name: gradient-backed sites are written into the baseline, so every one reports NO LONGER SCORED forever
edits:
return {"samples": {sample_key(s): s["ratio"]
                        for s in samples if not s.get("bg_uncertain")},

return {"samples": {sample_key(s): s["ratio"]
                        for s in samples},
expect: a gradient-backed site is NOT written into the baseline

name: main() resolves its corpus from the MODULE root instead of the one it was given, so a case cannot build the world it measures
expect: main() measures exactly the pages of the world it was GIVEN, not the repo's
...and a DIFFERENT world yields a DIFFERENT page list, so `root` is READ

name: the measurement stops being handed the root it was given (backlog #239's half), so the probe is looked for in the repo rather than the constructed world
expect: ...and FORWARDS that same world to the measurement — backlog #239's half
...and the forwarded root tracks that second world too

name: the success line drops its denominator and reverts to the pre-round-3 wording, so a 54%-coverage green reads as whole-corpus again
edits: print(f"  OK over {_cov} — no element crossed below AA and none already failing got worse")
print("  OK — no element crossed below AA and none already failing got worse")
expect: ...and the SUCCESS LINE names the fraction of baseline it covered
...and names it as 100%, a different number from the same code path

name: the NOT A WHOLE-CORPUS PASS warning fires on the wrong population — silent when the run was partial, loud when it was complete
expect: ...and says NOT A WHOLE-CORPUS PASS, so it cannot read as whole-corpus
...and stays SILENT about partiality rather than warning always
